summary: Bitten by serpents in the wilderness, the people are healed by looking at a bronze serpent Moses sets on a pole.

context.title: The bronze serpent
paragraphs: The episode closes the stories of Israel complaining in the wilderness, and the remedy comes through the very thing that wounds. [c1] The Gospel of John takes up the lifted serpent as an image of the Son of Man lifted up. [c2]

translationNotes.summary: Hebrew names the bronze serpent with two words that sound alike, nəḥaš nəḥōšeṯ.
translationNotes.body: The noun for serpent and the noun for bronze share their consonants, so the healing image echoes the danger it answers. English keeps the sense and loses the sound. [c3]

claims.text: Numbers 21:4-9 is one of the wilderness stories of the people complaining against God and Moses.
John 3:14 compares the lifting up of the Son of Man with Moses lifting up the serpent.
The Hebrew words nachash (serpent) and nechoshet (bronze) are a play on sound.

sources.citation: Brown, Driver and Briggs, A Hebrew and English Lexicon of the Old Testament, s.v. נְחֹשֶׁת
